summary: This note is a wiki-style article on presbycusis, the progressive, irreversible, bilateral age-related sensorineural hearing loss, most marked at high frequencies. It covers symptoms, causes (physiologic aging, sociocusis from everyday noise, and nosocusis such as ototoxic drugs, vascular disease, smoking, and diabetes), four pathological phenotypes, diagnosis by audiometry and tympanometry, and treatments including cochlear implants, middle ear implants, hearing aids, and experimental drug and stem cell research. It also notes that many non-mammal vertebrates regenerate cochlear sensory cells and avoid the condition.
one_line: Presbycusis is the progressive, irreversible age-related sensorineural hearing loss, its causes, phenotypes, diagnosis, treatments and research.
key_facts: Presbycusis is the cumulative effect of aging on hearing and is a progressive and irreversible bilateral symmetrical age-related sensorineural hearing loss.
The hearing loss of presbycusis is most marked at higher frequencies.
Presbycusis is the most common cause of hearing loss, affecting one out of three persons by age 65 and one out of two by age 75.
Presbycusis is the second most common illness next to arthritis in aged people.
The risk of cognitive impairment increased 7 percent for every 10 dB of hearing loss at baseline.
In the Framingham cohort study, only 10% of the variability of hearing with age could be explained by age-related physiologic deterioration.
Sociocusis is hearing loss attributed to continuous non-occupational noise exposures such as traffic, home appliances, music, television and radio.
Nosocusis factors that can cause hearing loss include ototoxic drugs like aspirin, vascular degeneration, smoking, diabetes and hypertension.
There are four pathological phenotypes of presbycusis: sensory, neural, strial/metabolic and cochlear conductive, plus mixed and indeterminate types.
The mainstay of sensorineural hearing loss is strial, with only about 5% of cases being sensory.
Normal hearing thresholds are considered to be 25 dB, though it has been proposed that 15 dB is more typical.
Mild hearing loss is defined as thresholds of 25–45 dB; moderate as 45–65 dB; severe as 65–85 dB; and profound as greater than 85 dB.
At present, presbycusis cannot be prevented, ameliorated or cured, and there are no approved or recommended pharmaceutical treatments for it.
A cochlear implant is possible for severe or profound hearing loss, electrodes typically being inserted through the round window into the scala tympani.

Many vertebrates such as fish, birds and amphibians do not experience presbycusis because they can regenerate their cochlear sensory cells, whereas mammals including humans have genetically lost this ability.

entities.name: Presbycusis
entities.role: age-related sensorineural hearing loss that is the subject of the note

entities.name: Framingham cohort study
entities.role: study in which only 10% of age-related hearing variability was explained by physiologic deterioration

entities.name: Lin Baltimore study
entities.role: study in which hearing aids showed no effect on cognitive impairment risk

entities.name: ISO standard 7029
entities.role: standard showing expected threshold changes due purely to age in carefully screened populations

entities.name: Tanakan
entities.role: prescription drug studied for treating tympanophonia and presbycusis in elderly patients

entities.name: AM-111
entities.role: otoprotective peptide shown in a chinchilla study to protect against hearing loss after impulse noise trauma

entities.name: Ebselen
entities.role: anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidant substance observed in a 2007 study to reduce noise-induced hearing loss in rats

entities.name: The Mosquito
entities.role: technology used to disperse groups of young people around shops by emitting high-frequency tones

entities.name: Teen Buzz
entities.role: cell phone ringtone for students that older people cannot hear

entities.name: Samp1 mice
entities.role: murine model of human senescence used in stem cell and thymus graft research

entities.name: CBA/J female mice
entities.role: animals placed on an antioxidant-rich diet in a 2012 study that did not improve hearing
